description: Routing evals for deciding when bugfix work needs a reusable postmortem and for enforcing postmortem content quality.

cases.prompt: I fixed a regression where the checkout total was computed incorrectly. Write the postmortem with root cause, fix, verification, and prevention.
cases.expected_output: Should load this skill and produce a structured postmortem covering symptom, impact, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention.
expectations: Treats the task as defect correction
Adds a Docs link from affected L2 AGENTS.md when present

cases.prompt: A broken test revealed a real caching defect. Capture the incident so future engineers understand what failed.
cases.expected_output: Should load this skill because the broken test exposed a real defect and the task asks for reusable root-cause knowledge.
expectations: Distinguishes real defects from test-only issues

cases.prompt: I refactored the settings module without changing behavior. Do I need a postmortem?
cases.expected_output: Should not load this skill as a mandatory postmortem generator because the work is behavior-preserving refactor only.
expectations: Recognizes non-defect refactors as out of scope

cases.prompt: Place this postmortem in the correct repo folder, name it, and update indexes.
cases.expected_output: Should prefer fractal-repo for placement, naming, and indexing, while postmortem remains responsible for content standards if needed.
expectations: Does not take primary ownership of repository placement

cases.prompt: I added a new sharing feature and also cleaned up two old warnings. Write a postmortem.
cases.expected_output: Should question whether the work is truly defect-led and consult decision rules rather than assuming every mixed task needs a postmortem.
expectations: Uses decision rules for borderline cases
Avoids over-triggering on mixed feature work

cases.prompt: The service went down in staging because of a bad env fallback. We fixed it and want a reusable incident record.
cases.expected_output: Should load this skill and produce an incident-style postmortem with impact, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention.
